title: United States announces funding for Caribbean regional initiatives
excerpt: The State Department announced new investments in undersea cables, healthcare, and security programs following a dialogue with Caribbean nations.
bodyHtml:
The United States State Department announced on October 16, 2026, that it is launching several initiatives to expand cooperation with Caribbean nations. This follows a U.S.-Caribbean Dialogue hosted by Deputy Secretary of State Landau on October 15, 2026, which included delegations from 15 Caribbean countries.

The Department of State announced $175.8 million to expand trusted, high-speed undersea cable connectivity across the Caribbean and Central America. Additionally, the Department of State intends to provide $61.5 million through the Americas Strategic Partnership for Independent Regional Healthcare Excellence to help Caribbean governments build self-sufficient health workforces.

The Department of State announced $37 million in CBSI programming to secure critical digital infrastructure and ports, and counter illegal, unreported, and unregulated fishing. Furthermore, the State Department announced $66 million in CBSI programming to strengthen Caribbean partners’ ability to counter transnational criminal organizations and secure the region’s borders. The Department of State announced that it will host a Caribbean Investment Summit in early 2027 to connect U.S. companies, financiers, and government finance agencies with Caribbean partners.
